issues.evidence: The cited NBS National Economy October release at https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202611/t20261116_1965843.html supports the October industrial PPI increase of 5.7%, industrial purchasing-price increase of 7.9% and the bureau's strong-supply/weak-demand statement, but it does not report the 18.6% fuel-and-power purchasing-price sub-index. The claim-specific primary source is the separate NBS release 'Industrial Producer Price Indexes in October 2026', published 10 November 2026, at https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202611/t20261111_1965806.html; it reports fuel and power purchasing prices up 18.6% year on year and 4.1% month on month. The number is correct; the cited source is incomplete.
issues.required_correction: Add the claim-specific NBS Industrial Producer Price Indexes in October 2026 release as a separate numbered reference in both editions and cite it immediately after the 18.6% claim. Keep reference [5] for the macro release and its strong-supply/weak-demand statement. Recalculate the source inventory and source count in the pending sidecar, then resubmit with new exact pending and EN/PT-BR blob SHAs.

locations: en.md:129, sentence reporting a 52 million barrel increase in observed inventories
pt-BR.md:129, sentence reporting a 52 million barrel increase in observed inventories
issues.evidence: The IEA November 2026 Oil Market Report at https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026 says observed inventories rose 52 mb in October because oil on water surged by 86 mb to its highest level since January. It also says on-land stocks continued to fall and remained at their lowest level since at least 2016, while OECD total stocks declined by 47 mb and industry inventories by 41 mb. The staged editions report only the +52 mb aggregate. In an analysis that uses inventory change to interpret the crude/product split, omitting the composition materially obscures why a higher observed total coexists with continued physical tightness.
issues.required_correction: Qualify the 52 mb aggregate with the IEA's composition: +86 mb oil on water, continued decline in on-land stocks to the lowest level since at least 2016, and the 47 mb OECD stock decline (41 mb industry inventories). Explain that the observed total increase does not demonstrate a broad recovery in accessible on-land inventories. Preserve the IEA's measurement window and units in both editions.

locations: en.md:129, sentence 'tight diesel supply, with prices near US$180 per barrel and freight costs elevated.'
pt-BR.md:129, sentence 'oferta apertada de diesel, com preços próximos de US$ 180 por barril e custos de frete elevados.'
issues.evidence: The IEA November 2026 Oil Market Report at https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026 identifies severe product-supply tightness, especially diesel, but the near-US$180/bbl price is specifically European diesel, which had fallen 11% over the period while remaining 77% above pre-war levels. The near-record freight statement concerns crude moving from the Middle East to Asia; the same release says Aframax and Suezmax costs eased. The staged wording removes these geographic and operational qualifiers and can be read as a global diesel price and a uniform freight-cost increase.
issues.required_correction: State explicitly that the near-US$180/bbl observation is European diesel and identify the IEA's reference period; distinguish it from the global product-supply assessment. Specify that Middle East-to-Asia crude freight rates remained near record levels while Aframax and Suezmax costs eased. Do not generalize either observation to all diesel markets or all freight classes.

issues.evidence: The pending sidecar classifies war-armed-conflict. The cited Reuters market report at https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/tech-leads-global-stocks-rout-treasury-yields-fall says crude prices rose late on 20 November on worries about possible attacks in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. The cited IEA report at https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026 reports ongoing attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers, Gulf exports of 18.4 mb/d (26% below pre-war levels), crude flows of 15 mb/d (82% of pre-war levels), and a cumulative 462 mb decline in observed global stocks since the start of the war. The staged body reduces this material transmission to generic 'geopolitical channels' and a conditional risk of disruption without identifying the source-attributed conflict or separating reported attacks from measured supply effects. CONFLICT-SECURITY-SOCIAL-CHANGE.md requires attribution of stated objectives/claims, separation of claims from verified effects and an evidenced transmission mechanism.
issues.required_correction: In both editions, attribute Reuters' report that crude rose on concerns about possible attacks in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. Attribute to the IEA its reporting of ongoing attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers, and distinguish those reports from measured effects such as Gulf export volumes and the pre-war comparison. Do not assert that the war alone explains the price move. If the conflict is not to be analyzed as a material cross-cutting phenomenon, remove war-armed-conflict from pending metadata and keep the energy risk explicitly conditional.
